'''Oscar Joshua Boone''' (born November 21, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. A 6'10" (2.08 m) [[power forward]]-[[Center (basketball)|center]], he played three years of college basketball for [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|UConn]]. He declared for the [[2006 NBA draft]] after his junior season, forgoing his final year of college.

==High school==
Born in [[Mount Airy, Maryland]], he attended [[South Carroll High School]] in [[Sykesville, Maryland]], where he averaged 20 points, 14.4 rebounds and seven blocked shots per game. He teamed with Indiana-bound [[Marshall Strickland]] to lead South Carroll to a 20–6 record. In his junior year, the team tied Governor Thomas Johnson High School for the league championship. South Carroll then lost in the regional semi-finals to top-ranked Paint Branch High School. The next year, he helped lead the team to only the school's second ever state final four appearance, losing to Gwynn Park in the final four.  After graduating, he attended [[West Nottingham Academy]] (a small college prep school) in [[Colora, Maryland]], averaging 28 points, 16 rebounds and 9.7 blocks per game.

==College==

===Freshman===
Boone played college basketball for [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] and was named to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Rookie Team. Started 37 of 38 games at power forward. Averaged 5.9 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.7 blocks, and shot .554 from the field, for [[NCAA]] Champion Huskies. Scored nine points in both [[Final Four#Final Four|Final Four]] games, and grabbed 14 rebounds in National Semifinal win over Duke. Averaged 8.0 points and 11.3 rebounds in three Big East Tournament games. Set a Big East Tourney record for rebounds in a game by a freshman with a career-high{{Citation needed|date=January 2009}} 16 boards in quarterfinal win at Notre Dame.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=240710041|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040515194301/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=240710041|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 15, 2004|title=Notre Dame vs. Connecticut - Game Recap - March 11, 2004 - ESPN|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> In the Huskies season opener vs. [[Yale]], became the 12th freshman under [[Jim Calhoun]] to start the season opener.

===Sophomore===
Big East Defensive Player of the Year and All-Big East Second Team selection. Named NABC and USBWA All-District First Team. Started all 31 games at center. Averaged 12.4 points, 8.4 rebounds and 2.9 blocks. Recorded a [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-double]] in 11 games. He registered 18 points and 15 rebounds in 75–70 loss to [[Boston College]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=250050041|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050306091405/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=250050041|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2005|title=Boston College vs. Connecticut - Game Recap - January 5, 2005 - ESPN|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> Scored a career-high 22 points and 8 blocked shots in the December 30, 2004 win over Quinnipiac.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=243650041|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102232837/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=243650041|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 2, 2012|title=Quinnipiac vs. Connecticut - Game Recap - December 30, 2004 - ESPN|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> He topped his career-high with nine blocks, along with seven points and eight rebounds, in win over St. John's on February 5, 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=250360041|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050306151812/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=250360041|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2005|title=St John's vs. Connecticut - Game Recap - February 5, 2005 - ESPN|work=ESPN.com}}</ref>

===Junior===
All-Big East Honorable Mention and NABC All-District Second Team selection. Started 32 of 34 games at the power forward position. Averaged 10.3 points, 7.0 rebounds and 2.0 blocks. He had eight double-doubles on the season. Tallied 13 points, 11 rebounds and two blocks in a 98–92 Sweet 16 win over Washington on March 24, 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=264000022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120926175723/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=264000022|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 26, 2012|title=Washington vs. Connecticut - Game Recap - March 24, 2006 - ESPN|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> Had 12 points, 14 rebounds and four blocks in a narrow 75–74 win over [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame]] on February 21, 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=260520041|title=Notre Dame vs. Connecticut - Game Recap - February 21, 2006 - ESPN|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> Recorded 17 points and 15 rebounds in a 66–53 win at South Florida on March 1, 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=260600058|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060321012953/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=260600058|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 21, 2006|title=Connecticut vs. South Florida - Game Recap - March 1, 2006 - ESPN|work=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===NBA===
Boone was picked 23rd overall in the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[New Jersey Nets]]. He was picked right behind former [[UConn]] teammate, [[Marcus Williams (UConn)|Marcus Williams]] who was also selected by the Nets. During the 2006 Pepsi Pro Summer League in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]] he led the league in rebounding (9 rpg) and was 2nd in blocked shots (1.67 bpg).

After the summer league he underwent surgery to repair a torn [[Glenoidal labrum|labrum]] in his left shoulder and was expected to be out for 4–6 months, however he returned much earlier. Boone made his NBA debut December 2, 2006, against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], playing 2 minutes. Suffering the effects of the injury and missing the pre-season training, Boone had an inconsistent but promising rookie season.

Boone averaged 4.2 points per game, 2.80 rebounds per game and 0.3 blocks per game during his rookie season. On December 26, 2006, he had a season-high of 12 rebounds against the [[Detroit Pistons]], a game in which he played 30 minutes, the most he had played hitherto. Boone had a then career-high 21 points on 10-for-10 shooting, while grabbing six rebounds on March 24, 2007, against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] in Charlotte. The following game, on March 28 against the Indiana Pacers, Josh eclipsed his previous career-high by scoring 22 points on 11-for-13 shooting. He also posted his first [[double-double]] by grabbing 10 rebounds.

In late December 2007, Boone earned a spot in the starting lineup. He replaced [[Jason Collins]] as the starting center and contributed immediately, putting up a double-double almost every night. During the month of January, Boone was the target of a "[[Hack-a-Shaq]]" by [[Golden State Warriors]] coach [[Don Nelson]], in which a player is intentionally fouled repeatedly to take advantage of his poor foul shooting. That season, Boone was second-worst in the NBA in free-throw percentage among players with at least one hundred attempts, at 45.6%<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/stats/player?season=2008&seasontype=2|title=2007-08 Regular Season NBA Player Stats and League Leaders - Free-Throws - National Basketball Association - ESPN|work=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Boone would see fewer minutes with the Nets, in part due to his free throw shooting. His accuracy at the line continued to deteriorate, as he hit 37.6% in 2008–09 and 32.8% in 2009–10. Only one player in the league with at least ten attempts had a lower percentage, [[Andris Biedrins]], who made four of twenty-five attempts.

===Post-NBA===
After not being re-signed by the Nets, Boone signed to play with the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] of China,<ref>[https://www.espn.com/blog/truehoop/post/_/id/31231/dwight-howard-to-china-josh-boones-scouting-report Dwight Howard to China? Josh Boone's scouting report] Chris Sheridan, ESPN.com, July 22nd, 2011.</ref> with whom he would play for parts of three seasons.

On January 17, 2013, Boone was acquired by the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA D-League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/energy_sign_former_nba_1st_rou_2013_01_17.html|title=NBA Development League: Energy Sign Former NBA 1st Round Pick Josh Boone|work=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 26, after he had played in only two games, it was announced that Boone would miss the rest of the 2012–13 season with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/josh_boone_out_for_season_with_2013_01_28.html|title=NBA Development League: JOSH BOONE OUT FOR SEASON WITH INJURY|work=NBA.com}}</ref>

In February 2014, Boone signed with the [[San Miguel Beermen]] as an import for the [[2014 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.inquirer.net/146380/san-mig-coffee-mixers-capture-ph-cup-crown|title=San Mig Coffee Mixers capture PH Cup crown|author=June Navarro|date=27 February 2014 }}</ref> He left the next month after just 2 games.

On March 22, 2014, Boone was re-acquired by the Iowa Energy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/energy-acquire-josh-boone/n-4755114|title=Energy Acquire Josh Boone|date=March 22, 2014|website=OurSports Central}}</ref>

In September 2014, Boone signed with [[Manama Club (basketball)|Manama]] of the [[Bahraini Premier League (basketball)|Bahraini Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/josh-boone-joins-al-manama/|title=Josh Boone joins Al Manama|author=Erik|work=Court Side Basketball News|date=9 September 2014 }}</ref> He went on to help Manama win their 19th championship in May 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gulf-daily-news.com/NewsDetails.aspx?storyid=402715|title=Manama claim league crown|publisher=Gulf Daily News}}</ref>

On September 9, 2015, Boone signed with [[BC Kalev/Cramo]] of Estonia.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/estonia/175334/josh-boone-signs-with-kalevcramo.html|title=Josh Boone signs with Kalev/Cramo|date=9 September 2015|work=Sportando}}</ref>

On January 13, 2016, Boone signed with [[BC Khimki]] of Russia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bckhimki.com/|title=Basketball Club Khimki|website=bckhimki.com}}</ref> He was supposed to replace injured Paul Davis and Ruslan Pateev.

On August 2, 2016, Boone signed with [[Pınar Karşıyaka]] of Turkey for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Karsiyaka adds big man Josh Boone|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/transfers/291204/karsiyaka-adds-big-man-josh-boone|access-date=August 2, 2016|work=Eurohoops.net|date=August 2, 2016}}</ref> On October 24, 2016, he parted ways with Karşıyaka after appearing in only one game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/215296/pinar-karsiyaka-and-josh-boone-officially-part-ways.html|title=Pinar Karsiyaka and Josh Boone officially part ways|work=Sportando }}</ref>

On December 24, 2016, Boone signed with [[Melbourne United]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] as an injury replacement player.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.melbourneutd.com.au/featured-news/josh-boone-unites-melbourne/|title=JOSH BOONE UNITES WITH MELBOURNE|work=MelbourneUtd.com.au|date=December 24, 2016|access-date=December 25, 2016|archive-date=December 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161225134249/http://www.melbourneutd.com.au/featured-news/josh-boone-unites-melbourne/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On February 21, 2017, Boone signed with the [[Eastern Sports Club (basketball)|Hong Kong Eastern Long Lions]] of the [[ASEAN Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/226665/josh-boone-inks-with-hong-kong-eastern-long-lions.html|title=Josh Boone inks with Hong Kong Eastern Long Lions|work=Sportando }}</ref> He helped the Long Lions win the championship after they defeated the [[Singapore Slingers]] in the ABL Finals.

On April 28, 2017, Boone re-signed with Melbourne United for the [[2017–18 NBL season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.melbourneutd.com.au/more-news/boone-is-back/|title=JOSH BOONE IS BACK|access-date=April 28, 2017|archive-date=April 29, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170429001857/http://www.melbourneutd.com.au/more-news/boone-is-back/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On August 14, 2018, he re-signed with United for the [[2018–19 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/43328-melbourne-re-sign-championship-duo|title=Melbourne Re-Sign Championship Duo|work=NBL.com.au|date=August 14, 2018|access-date=August 14, 2018}}</ref>

On May 21, 2019, Boone signed with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] for [[2019–20 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/josh-boone-signs-with-the-illawarra-hawks|title=Josh Boone Signs with the Illawarra Hawks|work=NBL.com.au|date=May 21, 2019|access-date=May 21, 2019}}</ref>

On March 4, 2020, he has signed with Al Nasr of the [[UAE National Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/josh-boone-signs-with-nasr-club/|title=Josh Boone signs with Nasr Club|date=March 4, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=March 5, 2020|last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola }}</ref> Boone signed with Al Riffa of the [[Bahraini Premier League (basketball)|Bahraini Premier League]] on August 9.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bahrain's Al Riffa signs Josh Boone |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/bahrains-al-riffa-signs-josh-boone/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 9, 2020 |date=August 9, 2020|last1=Borghesan |first1=Ennio Terrasi }}</ref>

In November 2021, it was announced Boone was on the roster of Canadian club [[Edmonton Stingers]] to strengthen their team for their maiden [[BCL Americas]] campaign in the [[2021–22 BCL Americas|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=CEBL Announces Training Camp Roster Ahead Of BCLA |url=https://www.thestingers.ca/stingers_bcla_roster |access-date=11 December 2021 |work=www.thestingers.ca |date=29 November 2021 |language=en}}</ref>
